buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at

the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Scope of Supply Scope of supply (Bid price to include all cost components) : Supply Installation Testing Commissioning of Goods and Training of operators and providing Statutory Clearances required (if any) 3. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Terms & Conditions (STC) 1. OEM Eligibility, Financial Thresholds & Experience • Absolute Manufacturing & Delivery Capability: The bidder must submit an unequivocal, irrevocable undertaking from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certifying that they possess the unencumbered manufacturing infrastructure, logistics, and capacity required to deliver the tendered items in full, without deviation or delay. • Defence Personnel Training Credentials: The OEM must provide authentic, institutional certification proving they have successfully trained a minimum of 500 Army / Defence / Civil Personnel at their authorized centres, failing which the bidder shall be deemed technically non-responsive. • OEM Should have training experience with Indian Armed Forces on Anti UAS Jammer within Last 1 Year. 2. Mandatory Technical Documentation & Disclosures • Comprehensive Project Execution Blueprint: The bidder must embed a granular, legally binding Project Management Plan directly within the tender document, explicitly detailing the execution methodology, critical paths, milestone timelines, and resource deployment strategies to guarantee project completion. • Authentic Datasheets & Component Schematics: The technical bid must include exhaustive, OEM-authenticated product datasheets accompanied by detailed physical and structural diagrams; any missing, obfuscated, or incomplete technical variables shall lead to absolute and immediate rejection of the entire bid. • Component-Level Country of Origin Disclosure: For all communication-based items and sub-systems, it is mandatory for the seller to provide a comprehensive

Bill of Materials (BOM) explicitly detailing the exact Country of Origin (CoO) down to the component and integrated circuit level; omissions will trigger immediate disqualification. 3. Statutory Certifications & Regulatory Compliance • Mandatory WPC System Certification: The proposed integrated system must possess a valid Equipment Type Approval (ETA) issued by the Wireless Planning & Coordination (WPC) Wing of the Ministry of Communications, and the physical certificate must be enclosed within the technical bid as a mandatory pre- requisite. • Import Compliance & ETA Documentation: The OEM assumes sole and absolute responsibility to submit valid, official ETA certificates at the technical evaluation stage for all imported items and components; failure to produce these documents will render the items non-compliant and the bid invalid. • Documentary Pre-qualification Bar: Bidders or OEMs who do not possess the complete set of required statutory certifications, regulatory approvals, and compliance documents at the exact time of bid submission are strictly prohibited from participating. 4. Technical Evaluation Committee (TEC) & Live Demonstration Protocols • Post-Technical Live Demonstration: Bidders successfully clearing the preliminary paperwork must undergo a rigorous, comprehensive physical demonstration of all proposed products before the Technical Evaluation Committee (TEC) at the designated evaluation stage. • Absolute Disqualification Framework: Any functional failure, specification mismatch, or performance deviation observed by the TEC during the live demonstration shall result in immediate, irreversible disqualification, with the TEC holding final, binding authority to confirm compliance. • Pre-Participation Product Possession: Bidders and OEMs must have ready, commercially operational units of the tendered products in their physical possession at the time of bidding; companies utilizing prototypes, conceptual designs, or lacking immediate demonstration capabilities are strictly barred from participation. . 4.
